subject: Principles of Accounting
generalObjectives: Stimulate and sustain candidates' interest in Principles of Accounting.
Use basic principles, knowledge and practical skills in Financial Accounting.
Apply the knowledge and interpretation of Accounting information to decision making.
Appreciate the relevance of Accounting information to business and governments.
Apply information technology in solving Accounting problems.

sections.sectionTitle: Section A: Nature and Principles of Accounting

topics.title: Nature and Significance of Book Keeping and Accounting
subtopics: Development of Accounting, including branches of accounting
Objectives of Book Keeping and Accounting
Users and characteristics of Accounting information
Principles, concepts and conventions of Accounting: nature, significance and application
Role of Accounting records and information
Career opportunities in Book Keeping and Accounting
objectives: Differentiate between Book Keeping and Accounting.
Understand the historical background of Book Keeping and Accounting.
Apply the right principles, concepts and conventions to solving Accounting problems.
Understand the role of Accounting information in decision making.

Identify the types and branches of Accounting, including Cost Accounting, Management Accounting, Auditing, Financial Accounting, Forensic Accounting, Social and Environmental Accounting, Government Accounting and Taxation.
Identify the different career opportunities in Book Keeping and Accounting.

topics.title: Principles of Double Entry
objectives: Identify various source documents and their uses.
Relate source documents to the various books of original entry.
Determine the effect of changes in elements of the Accounting equation.
Understand the role of double-entry principles in treating financial transactions.
Extract a trial balance from ledger accounts.
Identify various types of errors and their corrections.
Correct errors using a suspense account.

topics.title: Ethics, Professional and Regulatory Bodies in Accounting
objectives: Understand the ethics required in preparing and presenting Accounting information.
Understand qualities of an Accountant such as honesty, integrity, transparency, accountability and fairness.
Understand the purpose and functions of Accounting professional bodies in Nigeria.

Understand the purpose and functions of Accounting regulatory bodies in Nigeria, such as the Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria (FRCN), Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) and International Accounting Standards Board (IASB).

topics.title: Cash Book
subtopics: Petty Cash Book and imprest system
objectives: Determine the cash float.
Differentiate between two-column and three-column cash books and explain how transactions are recorded in them.
Differentiate between trade and cash discounts.
Examine the effects of trade and cash discounts in the books of accounts.
Identify various petty cash expenses.

topics.title: Bank Transactions and Reconciliation Statements
subtopics: Causes of discrepancies between cash book and bank statement
objectives: Identify various instruments of bank transactions, such as cheques, pay-in-slips, credit cards, debit cards and internet banking, and explain their uses.
Assess the impact of automated credit systems, credit transfers, interbank transfers and direct debit on cash balances.
Identify factors that cause discrepancies between cash book balance and bank statement.
Determine the adjusted cash book balance.

topics.title: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader or Proprietor
subtopics: Statement of profit or loss or income statement
Provision for bad and doubtful debt
Provision for depreciation using straight-line and reducing-balance methods
objectives: Determine the cost of sales, gross profit and net profit of a sole trader.
Identify non-current assets, current assets, long-term liabilities, current liabilities and proprietor's capital.
Compute adjustable items relating to expenditure and income in the statement of profit or loss.
Differentiate between bad debts and provision for bad and doubtful debts.

sections.sectionTitle: Section B: Stock, Control and Specialised Accounts

topics.title: Stock Valuation
subtopics: Meaning and purpose of stock valuation
Methods of stock valuation, including FIFO, LIFO and simple average
Advantages and disadvantages of the methods
objectives: Determine the value of materials issued to the production department using FIFO, LIFO and simple average.
Calculate the closing stock of materials or finished goods using FIFO, LIFO and simple average.
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of each method of stock valuation.
Determine the effects of stock valuation on elements of the income statement.

topics.title: Control Accounts
subtopics: Meaning and uses of control accounts
objectives: Understand the meaning of control accounts.
Identify the uses of control accounts in a business enterprise.
Differentiate between sales ledger control account and purchases ledger control account.
Identify the entries in control accounts.

topics.title: Incomplete Records and Single Entry
subtopics: Meaning of incomplete records and single entry
Differences between incomplete records and single entry
Preparation of final accounts from incomplete records
Conversion of single entry to double entry
objectives: Understand and differentiate between incomplete records and single entry.
Determine proprietor's capital using a statement of affairs.
Determine sales, purchases, cash balances, debtors, creditors and expenses by converting single entry to double entry.
Use Accounting equations and gross and net profit percentages to determine cost of sales, gross profit and net profit.

topics.title: Manufacturing Accounts
objectives: Identify the reason for preparing a manufacturing account.
Calculate prime cost, overhead cost, production cost and total cost.
Determine the basis of cost apportionment among production, administration, selling and distribution.

topics.title: Accounts of Not-for-Profit-Making Organizations
objectives: Distinguish between profit-oriented and not-for-profit-making organizations.
Determine annual subscription, subscription in arrears and subscription in advance.
Compute cash balances, accumulated funds, surplus or deficit for the period.

topics.title: Departmental Accounts
subtopics: Departmental statement of profit or loss
objectives: Identify the reasons for preparing departmental accounts.
Determine the expenses and incomes attributable to departments.
Compute departmental profit or loss.
Understand the Accounting treatment of inter-departmental transfers.

topics.title: Branch Accounts
subtopics: Pricing methods and accounts maintained by head office
Reconciliation of branch and head office books
objectives: Understand the reasons for preparing branch accounts.
Differentiate between types of branches.
Calculate profit or loss from branches.
Reconcile differences between branch and head office accounts.

topics.title: Joint Venture Accounts
objectives: Identify the objectives and features of joint ventures.
Identify the forms of joint ventures.
Identify the Accounting procedures of joint ventures.
Determine the profit or loss of a joint venture.

sections.sectionTitle: Section C: Partnership and Company Accounts

topics.title: Partnership Accounts
subtopics: Partnership final accounts: profit or loss account
Partnership final accounts: statement of financial position
Admission or retirement of a partner
objectives: Understand the procedures for the formation of a partnership.
Identify the accounts maintained for a partnership business.
Determine the effects of admission and retirement of a partner.
Determine profit or loss on revaluation of assets.
Determine the partners' share of profit or loss on dissolution.

topics.title: Introduction to Company Accounts
subtopics: Final accounts of companies: statement of profit or loss
Final accounts of companies: statement of financial position
Distinction between capital and revenue reserves
objectives: Differentiate between types of companies.
Identify the procedures for accounting for the issue of shares and debentures.
Compute the elements of final accounts of companies.
Compute and interpret Accounting ratios such as current ratio, acid-test ratio and stock turnover.

sections.sectionTitle: Section D: Public Sector Accounting and Accounting Technology

topics.title: Public Sector Accounting
subtopics: Accounting basis in the public sector
Responsibilities and powers of the Accountant General
Responsibilities and powers of the Auditor General
Responsibilities and powers of the Minister of Finance
Responsibilities and powers of the Treasurer of Local Government
Current issues in public sector Accounting: Treasury Single Account (TSA)
Integrated Payroll and Personnel Information System (IPPIS)
objectives: Differentiate between public and private sector Accounting.
Identify the sources of government revenue.
Differentiate between capital and recurrent expenditure.
Calculate the Consolidated Revenue Fund and determine the values of assets and liabilities.
Identify the duties of the Accountant General, Auditor General, Minister of Finance and Treasurer of Local Government.
Distinguish between elements of control in government Accounting procedures, such as warrants, votes, budgets and due process certificates.
Understand current trends in public sector Accounting.

topics.title: Information Technology in Accounting
subtopics: Manual and computerized Accounting processing systems
Digitization and digital technologies in Accounting
objectives: Differentiate between manual and computerized Accounting processing systems.
Identify the procedures involved in data processing.
Identify the digital technologies used in Accounting processing systems.
Understand the benefits of blockchain technology in Accounting systems.
Identify services provided by virtual accountants, such as bookkeeping, payroll processing, tax preparation, bank, credit and loan account reconciliation, and financial statement preparation.
Identify the advantages and disadvantages of computerized Accounting processing systems.
